author: Aisha Kapoor

description: Context: A production incident on 2026-02-24 revealed a race between SLO enforcer backoff logic and regional failover that caused temporary over-shedding and a spike in 5xxs during sustained partial-region degradation. Root cause: two issues combined - (1) use of system clock for backoff math produced negative/incorrect backoff windows during host suspend/clock adjustments, and (2) non-atomic updates to in-flight counters allowed a failover state machine to trigger duplicate failover work and double-shed requests in the same window. This hotfix makes the backoff window monotonic-clock based and introduces atomic transitions/guards around regional failover to eliminate the race. Changes: - Replace wall-clock math with monotonic Instant for all backoff calculations. - Convert in-flight counters and failover state transitions to atomic CAS operations and add an explicit guard to ensure single failover per event. - Add regression and integration tests that reproduce the original race and verify fixed behavior under suspend/resume and delayed scheduling. - Expose a temporary helm feature flag sloEnforcer.strictBackoff to allow quick rollbacks if needed. CI: added a repro test that runs in the linux and linux/arm matrices. Rollout plan: merged to main, will be hot-patched to the 2026-02-24 release channel and monitored with a short-lived increased alerting window. Related: SUP-7821, ENG-4092. Notes: this is a low-risk code path change constrained to the SLO enforcer service but addresses a customer-impacting regression.
